clue.text: Effect sponsored nomination

parts.note: to effect is to bring about; the naming of a baby at baptism is done with godparents, formally called sponsors, standing for the child

explanation.surface: Someone pulls strings to get a backed candidate nominated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Effect' is a verb here (bring about), and 'sponsored' refers to the godparents who stand for a baby at baptism.
explanation.definitionFit: At a baptism the infant is given a name with godparents as sponsors, so performing that ceremony is bringing about a sponsored naming.

clue.text: Visitor fresh from Scotland

definitions.meaning: someone who calls at the house
in Scots dialect the word means fresh, as in newly caught herring

explanation.definitionFit: One who pays a call is a guest, and in Scots the same word describes fresh fish or cool air.

clue.text: Dominated police department — that's bad

parts.note: to run something is to control it, so dominated is ran
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Officers ran the detective squad, and that was a bad business.
explanation.walkthrough: CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off and smells sour, like old butter, is spoiled or bad.

clue.text: Establishes a section of reserves

parts.note: to set up or fix something is to set it
a part is a section of something

explanation.surface: A ruling creates a separate part of the reserve forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something aside for a special purpose is to hold it back or earmark it.

clue.text: Transport for former head of state and family

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
Pres is short for president, a head of state
a strain is a line of descent or breed, a family

explanation.surface: Arranging a car for a former president and his relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast passenger service stopping at few stations is a means of travel or conveyance.

clue.text: Maybe no clear guide to the future

parts.note: no is nothing, shown as the zero-like letter O

indicators.note: maybe suggests the following word could be something else, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Perhaps there is no clear path ahead to the future.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophetic source consulted for predictions, as at Delphi, serves as a guide to what is coming.

clue.text: Wine from a Spanish river gets OK in Germany

parts.note: rio is Spanish for river
ja is German for yes, agreement like OK

explanation.surface: A wine from a river region in Spain is approved by the Germans.
explanation.definitionFit: A red from the northern Spanish region of the same name, made largely from Tempranillo grapes.

clue.text: One of those powerful passages

parts.note: refers to the stock phrase about the hallways of government where influence is wielded

explanation.surface: A stirring paragraph in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Powerful passages' suggests forceful writing, but alludes to the phrase 'the corridors of power'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'corridors of power' names the hallways of government where influence is exercised.

clue.text: Begs hospital department in brief to revise rates

parts.note: ENT is short for ear, nose and throat, a hospital department

indicators.note: revising the word rates means altering its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A hospital unit pleads for a review of charges.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore or plead with someone earnestly is to beg them.

clue.text: It speeds composition of a kind of floor-cover

parts.note: lino, short for linoleum, is a floor covering
a type is a kind or sort

explanation.surface: A gadget that makes laying a certain floor covering quicker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composition' means typesetting: this machine casts whole lines of type, speeding the compositor's work.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot-metal typesetting machine casting whole lines at once, it greatly accelerated the setting of print.

clue.text: Amy has little entitlement to Dickens's output

definitions.text: Amy has little entitlement to Dickens's output

parts.words: Amy has little entitlement to Dickens's output
parts.note: Amy is the heroine of a Dickens novel, and the word Little forms part of the title, so she is literally entitled with 'Little'

explanation.surface: Poor Amy has scant claim on the money Dickens earned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little entitlement' means the title of the novel begins with 'Little', the nickname of its heroine Amy.
explanation.definitionFit: Amy is the title heroine of the Dickens novel named after her with the nickname Little.

clue.text: Firm, by first of May, hopeful of reaching settlement

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: first of takes just the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: promising means showing signs of future success, hopeful

explanation.surface: A company hopes to reach a deal by the start of May.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming to terms by mutual concessions is settling a dispute, so one doing so is agreeing to a middle way.

clue.text: Girl's name for a rice pudding ?

indicators.note: a pudding is a mixture, so these words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: What would you call a rice pudding if it were a girl?
explanation.walkthrough: The held text dropped 'for' and 'rice'; the page prints 'Girl's name for a rice pudding?'. 'Pudding' is a noun on the surface but signals mixing the letters of A RICE.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a feminine given name, also the botanical genus of heather.

clue.text: Note-case reviving memories

parts.note: E is a musical note
the vocative is a grammatical case, used in addressing someone

explanation.surface: A wallet for notes that brings back recollections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note-case' looks like a wallet, but splits into a musical note and a grammatical case.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that calls up past feelings and recollections is said to be redolent or suggestive of them.

clue.text: Framed perhaps by use of this master key ?

definitions.text: Framed perhaps by use of this master key ?

parts.words: Framed perhaps by use of this master key
parts.note: the French term for a master key also names the gummed tape or mount used for framing pictures

explanation.surface: A burglar fitted up by evidence of the master key he used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Framed' suggests being falsely accused, but here it is picture framing; the same French word means both a master key and a picture mount.
explanation.definitionFit: The French term for a key that opens every lock is also used for a passe-partout picture mount or binding tape.

clue.text: Check the following in what's left

indicators.note: in places the retinue word within the word for the remainder

parts.note: the rest is what remains
a train is a retinue, the people following someone important

explanation.surface: Inspect the next part of what remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The following' is a noun meaning a body of followers, a TRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-control or holding back is a check on action.

clue.text: Making a poor job of new sign outside military station

indicators.note: outside says the rearranged letters of sign wrap round the military word
new indicates the word sign is remade in a different order

parts.note: a camp is a place where troops are stationed

explanation.surface: Botching a fresh signpost outside an army base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making a poor job of' is a verb phrase: to scamp work is to skimp it. 'New' rearranges the letters of sign, and 'outside' wraps them round the station.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamp work is to do it hastily and carelessly, skimping it.

clue.text: Such a goose difficult to shake off?

definitions.meaning: a species of wild goose shares the name with a shellfish
a shellfish that clings to rocks and hulls, figuratively a clinging person; the adjective phrase describes such a hanger-on

explanation.definitionFit: The barnacle goose is a black and white Arctic species, and the clinging crustacean stands for a hanger-on hard to get rid of.

clue.text: Hire accommodation for school

parts.note: to charter a boat or plane is to hire it
a house is a dwelling, somewhere to be accommodated

explanation.surface: Renting rooms for a school.
explanation.walkthrough: CHARTERHOUSE is a famous English public (private boarding) school in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the name of a well-known English independent boarding school, founded in London in 1611.

clue.text: Foreign currency partly for internal use

indicators.note: partly says only some of the letters of the words for internal are used

explanation.surface: Some foreign money is kept for use at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface implies money spent at home, but the answer lies inside FOR INTernal.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the monetary unit of Hungary.

clue.text: Hide worker finding old coin

definitions.meaning: one who turns animal skins into leather
British slang for the pre-decimal sixpence

explanation.walkthrough: The sixpence was a small British silver coin before decimalisation in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: A leather-maker treats hides, and in old British slang a sixpenny piece had the same nickname.

clue.text: Ray gets one pound in return from Dickens's dressmaker …

parts.note: a manta is a large ray

indicators.note: return means the short words one, pound and in are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I
L stands for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A fish catches a pound in exchange from a Dickens character who makes dresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In return' reads in, one and pound backwards. The Mantalinis run a dressmaking business in Dickens's Nicholas Nickleby; the clue's trailing dots lead on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mantalinis keep a fashionable millinery and dressmaking shop in Dickens's Nicholas Nickleby.

clue.text: Didn't go, without saying I'm ere

definitions.text: Didn't go, without saying I'm ere

parts.words: Didn't go, without saying I'm ere
parts.note: at a school roll call a pupil who was present, not gone, answers with the Latin for I am here, dropped aitch and all

explanation.surface: A Cockney who stayed put made sure to announce it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin reply at roll call means 'I am present'; 'I'm 'ere' is a dropped-aitch rendering of that.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Latin response to a roll call meaning present, used in schools and colleges.

clue.text: … or had change from Miss Fleming

indicators.note: change tells you to alter the order of the two short words before it

explanation.surface: Continuing the story: or perhaps a dress needed altering for a Miss Fleming.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhoda Fleming is the title heroine of a novel by George Meredith.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoda Fleming is the heroine of George Meredith's 1865 novel bearing her full name.

clue.text: Put under cover as a precaution

definitions.meaning: to enclose something in a box or sheath, a variant spelling of encase
a phrase meaning just to be safe, should something happen

explanation.definitionFit: A variant of encase means to wrap or enclose, and read as two words the phrase means to guard against a possibility.

clue.text: Legal department of the army

parts.note: the High Court has sections such as Chancery, and an army is organised into large formations; both share one name

explanation.surface: The army's in-house lawyers.
explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a single unit of military lawyers, but the word fits both a branch of the High Court and an army formation.
explanation.definitionFit: The English High Court is split into Chancery, Family and King's Bench sections, and an army formation of several brigades has the same name.

clue.text: Shines as a novice in rough games

indicators.note: in places the learner's letter within the rearranged word games
rough games are disorderly, so their letters are jumbled

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate shown by learner drivers

explanation.surface: A beginner excels in some rough-and-tumble play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' turns GAMES into GAEMS, and 'in' puts L (novice) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To glimmer or glint is to give off light, the same as shining.
